title: swapbytes
summary: Reverse the byte order of numeric values.

gpu_support.notes: Automatic resident inputs gather transparently and preserve exact class and shape. Explicit gpuArray fallback is available only when RunMat extensions are enabled.

description: `swapbytes(X)` reverses the byte order of each numeric element while preserving the input numeric class.
behaviors: Supports scalar integer values and scalar doubles.
Supports dense `double`, `single`, and all eight native integer classes, including full-width `int64` and `uint64` values.
`uint8` values are unchanged because they contain one byte.
Floating-point values are reinterpreted by their IEEE bytes, byte-swapped, and returned in the same class.
Integer outputs preserve input class, shape, and exact byte-reversed values for all eight integer classes.
Logical, complex, string, cell, struct, and object inputs raise errors.
Automatically resident inputs gather transparently. Explicit gpuArray input uses the same host fallback only when RunMat extensions are enabled.

examples.description: Swap every element of an unsigned integer array

faqs.question: Does `swapbytes` preserve integer class?
faqs.answer: Yes. Every native integer class is byte-swapped directly in authoritative storage and returned with the same class and shape. Eight-bit values are unchanged because each element contains only one byte.

faqs.question: What happens with resident inputs?
faqs.answer: Automatic residency is transparent: RunMat gathers, swaps bytes exactly on the host, and returns the host result. An explicitly requested gpuArray fallback is an additional capability and requires RunMat extensions to be enabled.
